---
# There is deliberately no `title:` or `author:` here. Either one makes Quarto
# generate its own title slide, and that slide cannot be edited — you cannot put
# an image on it, reveal it in steps, or place anything by hand, and the CSS
# tricks that appear to work live stop working in the PDF, because reveal moves
# every slide into a different wrapper when it prints. Leave both out and Quarto
# builds no title slide at all, which makes slide 1 below yours.
#
# `pagetitle` still names the browser tab and the PDF. `date` reaches no slide
# on its own; the cover asks for it with {{< meta date >}}.
pagetitle: "Your talk title"
date: last-modified
date-format: "D MMMM YYYY"
bibliography: ref.bib
# Spoken over, or read alone? It decides how much belongs on a slide — the
# quarto-academic-style skill has the rest. Absent means speaker-led.
density: speaker-led   # or: reading-first
format:
  revealjs:
    footer: "Your Name (Your Institute) &nbsp;·&nbsp; Short talk title"
---

## {.cover}

     centre a short slide by pushing it down the page. That is what lets
     `.absolute` below measure from the slide's own corner and stay there

## Write here, build with `make`

:::: {.columns-1-1}

::: {.column}
::: {.no-header}
| | |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `##`        | a new slide                |
| `#`         | a section divider slide    |
| `---`       | another slide, same title  |
| `. . .`     | reveal the rest on a click |
| `::: notes` | speaker notes; press **S** |
:::
:::

::: {.column}
::: {.no-header}
| | |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `make`         | render `out/talk.html`       |
| `make preview` | reloads as you save          |
| `make check`   | catches content off the edge |
| `make png`     | one PNG per slide, to read   |
| `make all`     | HTML, PDF and PPTX           |
:::
:::

::::

::: {.highlight}
The look is one line of `_quarto.yml` — `theme: [default, themes/nord.scss]`.
All ten stylesheets travel inside this folder.
:::

::: notes
Nothing load-bearing goes in a notes block: reveal hides it in print, so it
reaches neither the PDF nor the PPTX. Press **S** for the presenter window —
notes, a timer, the next slide — and **X** to draw the slide boundary.
:::

## A figure is the slide, not an illustration

:::::: {.columns-2-3}

::::: {.column}
:::: {.small}

::: {.fragment}
Spoken over, this side is a claim and nothing more; the narration goes in
`::: notes`. Read alone, nobody is standing there to finish the sentence for
you, so the argument has to arrive whole — which is what `density:` in the
header decides.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- A point worth making, finished rather than left hanging
- One that needs an [emphasis]{.alert} to carry over the rest
- One that can stay [quieter]{.muted} without being cut
:::

::: {.fragment}
When a column has more to say than fits, wrap it in `.small` and the figure
keeps its size. At `0.78em` it still reads from the back of a room; `.tiny` at
`0.62em` does not, so save that for a source line.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Give an image a width **or** a height, never both. The aspect ratio is data —
stretch a figure and equal axes stop being square, while the result still looks
entirely plausible. Anything drawn more than 2% off the file's own shape fails
`make check`.
:::

::: {.highlight}
`.media-row` is a grid: label in one column, frames in the other. Set
`--label-width` once on a wrapper and every row lines up; `.fragment` on each
image walks the strip a frame at a time.

## Text, numbers, code and maths

:::: {.columns-1-1}

::: {.column}
#### Subheadings start at `####`

Body text with `inline code`, a [link](https://quarto.org) and **bold** where a
claim needs it. Maths is sized to the body, so $\bar{x} = n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$ sits
inside a sentence and a result gets its own line:

$$ \sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2 $$

> A sentence somebody else wrote, set as a blockquote.
:::

::: {.column}
| Method | Samples | Accuracy |
|:---------------|-------:|--------:|
| Baseline       |  1,000 |     71% |
| + new features |  1,000 |     84% |
| + more data    | 10,000 |     89% |

```python
def accuracy(correct, total):
    return correct / total
```

::: {.small}
`.small` for a block that has to give way, `.tiny` below that. The stylesheet
colours the code from its own palette, so the listing follows the theme.
:::
:::
